compile.schedule: interfaces ≫ finish ≫ load ≫ swap ≫ subtract ≫ clear

explain: Either order can do one swap and one subtract per cycle; the order only changes how they pair up. With swap ≫ subtract, a cycle swaps first and then subtracts from the swapped values. With subtract ≫ swap, it subtracts first and then swaps if the result fell below y. For gcd(48, 18), started at cycle 1, io_done rises at cycle 6 instead of 7: 5 cycles instead of 6, and both give 6. On other inputs the difference can go the other way.

+  schedule finish ≫ load ≫ subtract ≫ swap ≫ clear;

compile.schedule: interfaces ≫ finish ≫ load ≫ subtract ≫ swap ≫ clear

explain: swap and subtract both write x, so they cannot run in parallel. Their guards happen to be exclusive (x < y against x ≥ y), but ∥ requires disjoint write sets regardless of guards, so the front end rejects it.
